assumptions: \(E\) is a nonempty normed additive commutative group, with its Borel measurable structure, second-countable topology and a standard Borel measurable space. No vector-space or finite-dimensional structure is assumed.

\(\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3\) are probability measures on E. Couplings have exactly the two prescribed coordinate marginals. Define \[C(\gamma)=\left(\int\|x-y\|^2\,d\gamma(x,y)\right)^{1/2}.\] Both costs and \(W_2\) take values in \([0,\infty]\); \(W_2\) is the square root of the infimum of squared coupling costs.

The external thresholds \(r_{12},r_{23}\in[0,\infty]\) satisfy \[W_2(\mu_1,\mu_2)<r_{12},\qquad W_2(\mu_2,\mu_3)<r_{23}.\] Neither optimal-plan existence nor finite individual second moments is given.

/- SamplingOptimisationGeometryBench public-dev reference.
   Reuses the existing project proof; retain LICENSE and NOTICE. -/
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.TransportGluing
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinTriangleMarginals
import Mathlib.Tactic

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinTriangleCore
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinTriangleMarginals
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]
  [StandardBorelSpace E] [Nonempty E]

example
    (μ₁ μ₂ μ₃ : Measure E)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ₁] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ₂] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ₃]
    {r₁₂ r₂₃ : ℝ≥0∞}
    (hr₁₂ : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₂ < r₁₂)
    (hr₂₃ : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₂ μ₃ < r₂₃) :
    WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₃ < r₁₂ + r₂₃ := by
  rcases
      WassersteinSpace.exists_isCoupling_sqrt_lintegral_lt_of_wassersteinDistance_lt
        μ₁ μ₂ hr₁₂ with
    ⟨γ₁₂, hγ₁₂, hcost₁₂⟩
  rcases
      WassersteinSpace.exists_isCoupling_sqrt_lintegral_lt_of_wassersteinDistance_lt
        μ₂ μ₃ hr₂₃ with
    ⟨γ₂₃, hγ₂₃, hcost₂₃⟩
  rcases TransportGluing.exists_gluing_of_isCoupling γ₁₂ γ₂₃ hγ₁₂ hγ₂₃ with
    ⟨γ₁₂₃, hfst, hmap₂₃⟩

  have hmap₁₂ : Measure.map (pair12 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃ = γ₁₂ := by
    change Measure.map Prod.fst γ₁₂₃ = γ₁₂
    exact hfst
  have hmap₂₃' : Measure.map (pair23 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃ = γ₂₃ := by
    change Measure.map (fun p : ((E × E) × E) => (p.1.2, p.2)) γ₁₂₃ = γ₂₃
    exact hmap₂₃

  have hpair₁₂ :
      Transport.IsCoupling (Measure.map (pair12 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃) μ₁ μ₂ := by
    rw [hmap₁₂]
    exact hγ₁₂
  have hpair₂₃ :
      Transport.IsCoupling (Measure.map (pair23 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃) μ₂ μ₃ := by
    rw [hmap₂₃']
    exact hγ₂₃
  have hpair₁₃ :
      Transport.IsCoupling (Measure.map (pair13 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃) μ₁ μ₃ :=
    isCoupling_map_pair13_of_pair12_pair23 γ₁₂₃ hpair₁₂ hpair₂₃

  have hedge₁₂ :
      l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength12 (E := E)) =
        (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E) z ∂γ₁₂) ^
          (1 / (2 : ℝ)) := by
    rw [l2Seminorm_edge12_eq_pairCost, hmap₁₂]
  have hedge₂₃ :
      l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength23 (E := E)) =
        (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E) z ∂γ₂₃) ^
          (1 / (2 : ℝ)) := by
    rw [l2Seminorm_edge23_eq_pairCost, hmap₂₃']
  have hendpoint :
      WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₃ ≤
        l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength13 (E := E)) := by
    calc
      WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₃ ≤
          (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E) z
            ∂Measure.map (pair13 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ)) :=
        WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance_le_sqrt_lintegral_of_isCoupling
          μ₁ μ₃ (Measure.map (pair13 (E := E)) γ₁₂₃) hpair₁₃
      _ = l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength13 (E := E)) :=
        (l2Seminorm_edge13_eq_pairCost γ₁₂₃).symm

  calc
    WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₃ ≤
        l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength13 (E := E)) := hendpoint
    _ ≤ l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength12 (E := E)) +
          l2Seminorm γ₁₂₃ (edgeLength23 (E := E)) :=
      l2_edge_triangle γ₁₂₃
    _ = (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E) z ∂γ₁₂) ^
          (1 / (2 : ℝ)) +
        (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E) z ∂γ₂₃) ^
          (1 / (2 : ℝ)) := by rw [hedge₁₂, hedge₂₃]
    _ < r₁₂ + r₂₃ := ENNReal.add_lt_add hcost₁₂ hcost₂₃

    (hr₂₃ : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₂ μ₃ < r₂₃) :

mathematical_cores.question: Prove \(W_2(\mu_1,\mu_3)<r_{12}+r_{23}\) by choosing strictly near-optimal adjacent plans and gluing them over their common middle marginal. Identify the measure used in Minkowski, justify all three pair-marginal cost identities and explain the measurability/conditional-version requirements. Audit the shortcut \(\Gamma'=\gamma_{12}\otimes\mu_3\): use identical Bernoulli marginals and diagonal adjacent plans to show exactly which identification fails. Do not assume optimal-plan attainment or convert extended costs to real numbers.

rubric.criterion: Selects actual strictly near-optimal adjacent couplings and derives their probability interfaces without assuming attainment or individual finite second moments.
Constructs the common-middle conditional gluing with measurable kernels and both pair marginals, respecting the almost-everywhere meaning of conditional versions.
Uses measurable pushforward cost identities and extended L² Minkowski on one triple law to obtain the endpoint coupling bound and exact strict sum.

Gives the diagonal Bernoulli/independent-third-coordinate counterexample with discrepancy probability 1/2 and edge norm 1/√2, identifying a failed marginal/cost identity rather than claiming the true triangle inequality fails.

mathematical_cores.source_note: Original QA and counterexample explanation over the existing ASTIS-owned strict-threshold transport join and its source-present gluing, marginal and L² components. No textbook passage, paper text, external dataset or restricted index is reproduced. The exact-order consumer is AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinTriangleExact.wassersteinDistance_triangle. This composition family shares probability/coupling foundations with the earlier symmetry questions but is not a relabeled variant; all remain public-dev.
steps: Strict near-optimal selection gives actual couplings \(\gamma_{12},\gamma_{23}\) with \[C(\gamma_{12})<r_{12},\qquad C(\gamma_{23})<r_{23}.\] These are consequences of the transport infimum and positive square-root order, not an assumption that the infimum is attained. A coupling of a probability marginal has total mass one, so both plans are probability measures.

Disintegrate the second plan with respect to its first coordinate. The finite standard-Borel conditional-kernel theorem supplies a Markov version \(\kappa(y,dz)\) with \[\gamma_{23}(dy,dz)=\mu_2(dy)\kappa(y,dz).\] Define \[\Gamma(d(x,y),dz)=\gamma_{12}(dx,dy)\kappa(y,dz).\] Markov normalization preserves its first pair marginal. Equality \(\gamma_{12}.\mathrm{snd}=\mu_2=\gamma_{23}.\mathrm{fst}\), kernel measurability and the disintegration identity preserve the second pair marginal. Conditional representatives need only have the correct \(\mu_2\)-almost-everywhere meaning; an unsupported pointwise conditional formula is not used.

Write \(\pi_{ij}\) for the measurable pair projections from the same triple space. The identities are \[(\pi_{12})_\#\Gamma=\gamma_{12},\qquad(\pi_{23})_\#\Gamma=\gamma_{23}.\] Put \(\gamma_{13}=(\pi_{13})_\#\Gamma\). Composing measurable coordinate projections proves that its marginals are \(\mu_1,\mu_3\). The Borel norm and the product/projection measurability justify nonnegative pushforward integration; no subtraction of infinite integrals occurs.

For \(e_{ij}(x,y,z)=\|x_i-x_j\|\), all edge functions are measurable. Nonnegative pushforward integration gives \[\|e_{12}\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}=C(\gamma_{12}),\qquad\|e_{23}\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}=C(\gamma_{23}).\] The endpoint identity is \[\|e_{13}\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}=C(\gamma_{13}).\] Pointwise \(e_{13}\le e_{12}+e_{23}\) and extended-nonnegative L² Minkowski apply on this single law Γ, not on two unrelated pair spaces.

Using the endpoint coupling to bound the infimum, then the preceding identities, yields \[\begin{aligned}W_2(\mu_1,\mu_3)&\le C(\gamma_{13})\\&\le C(\gamma_{12})+C(\gamma_{23})\\&<r_{12}+r_{23}.\end{aligned}\] The coefficient is exactly one on each cost. Strict extended-order addition handles the thresholds without an infinity-minus-infinity operation. No optimal plan, density or individual second-moment assumption is added.

For the shortcut audit, take \(E=\mathbb R\) and all three marginals equal to \(\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\delta_1\), with both adjacent plans diagonal. Their costs are zero. Under \(\Gamma'=\gamma_{12}\otimes\mu_3\), Y and Z are independent, so \[\mathbb P_{\Gamma'}(Y\ne Z)=\tfrac12,\qquad\|e_{23}\|_{L^2(\Gamma')}=1/\sqrt2.\] Its second pair marginal is the independent product, not the diagonal \(\gamma_{23}\), and cannot have cost zero. This refutes the shortcut's cost identification, not the true Wasserstein inequality. Correct conditional gluing makes X=Y=Z in this example.
mathematical_cores.title: Gluing the right joint law before applying Minkowski

case-1.assumptions: E is a nonempty second-countable normed additive commutative group whose measurable structure is the Borel σ-algebra of its topology and which is a standard Borel space. The measures μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ are probability measures. The two numerical hypotheses are WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₂ < r₁₂ and WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₂ μ₃ < r₂₃. There are no separately assumed finite second moments or finite radii; each strict inequality itself forces its left-hand distance to be finite and its radius to be positive, while allowing that radius to be infinity.
case-1.conclusion: WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ₁ μ₃ < r₁₂ + r₂₃ in ℝ≥0∞. Thus any two strict radius bounds on the consecutive Wasserstein distances yield a strict bound on the endpoint distance by the sum of those radii. The asserted conclusion is this conditional strict bound, not a claim of equality or of an attained infimum, nor an assertion that the radii or their sum are finite. The conclusion does imply that the endpoint distance is finite.
case-1.constants: The transportation exponent is the fixed number 2, and its square root uses the fixed real exponent 1/2. Probability normalization fixes each measure's total mass to 1. The symbols r₁₂ and r₂₃ are universally quantified variable bounds, not fixed numerical constants; their sum occurs with coefficient 1 on each radius. No further numerical constants or dimension parameters appear.
case-1.domains: E is an arbitrary type with NormedAddCommGroup E, MeasurableSpace E, BorelSpace E, SecondCountableTopology E, StandardBorelSpace E, and Nonempty E. Each μᵢ belongs to Measure E and has total mass one. The radii r₁₂ and r₂₃ belong to ℝ≥0∞, the nonnegative extended real numbers, and the Wasserstein distances also take values there. No scalar or vector-space structure, finite-dimensionality, completeness, or finite-moment condition is required by the signature.
case-1.objects: A space E equipped with a normed additive commutative group structure and its specified measurable and topological structures; three probability measures μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ on E; two radii r₁₂, r₂₃; and the extended-valued quadratic Wasserstein distances between these measures.
case-1.quantifiers: Universally quantify over every E and all the listed structures on it, every triple μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ of probability measures on E, and every pair r₁₂, r₂₃ in ℝ≥0∞. For each such choice, if the two displayed strict inequalities hold, the displayed strict inequality for μ₁ and μ₃ follows. The type E and the radii are implicit Lean parameters, not existentially chosen objects.
case-1.senses: The distance between μ and ν is the nonnegative extended-real real-power square root of the infimum, over coupling measures γ on E × E with first marginal μ and second marginal ν, of the quadratic transportation cost ∫ ‖x − y‖² dγ. Costs, empty infima, comparisons, and the radius addition are interpreted in ℝ≥0∞, including infinity, rather than by ordinary real-valued conventions for divergent integrals. The norm is that of the additive group; no vector-space geometry or dimension restriction is implicit. The measurable structure is precisely Borel, and StandardBorelSpace is an additional stated measurable-space condition.
